result:
The proposed answer of $1+\ln 2$ is very likely wrong.

The derivation is heuristic. The comb construction gives explosion only for $p<4/3$. The jump from there to $1+\int_2^\infty \frac{dg}{g(g-1)}$ comes from an unjustified nesting-exponent argument. A threshold of $1+\ln 2$ would also be an unusual value for a sharp moment threshold of this kind.

I could not derive the true value here. From memory, the literature on divisible sandpile stabilization on bounded-degree graphs with i.i.d. masses gives a sharp threshold of $q=2$. Stabilization holds for finite $p$-th moment with $p>2$, and explosion examples exist for $p<2$. This recollection is not verified, but it disagrees with $1+\ln 2\approx 1.693$.

VERDICT: REJECT
